requirements.text: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk

outcomes.description: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
outcomes.target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show visual evidence of a chalk-like drawing treatment applied to the input image?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image visibly has a chalk-like drawing appearance; fail if there is sufficient evidence that it remains without a chalk-like drawing treatment; unknown if the image evidence is insufficient to determine this.
nodes.binding: Compare the edited image with the input image for a chalk-like drawing appearance. Judge the visible result, not a particular technique; unrelated edits do not count as progress.

nodes.question: Does the chalk-like drawing treatment transform the image as a whole, rather than appearing only as a partial effect?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the image as a whole is rendered as a chalk-made drawing; fail if sufficient evidence shows no chalk-drawing progress, or only a partial chalk effect; unknown if the evidence cannot establish whether the transformation is complete or partial.
nodes.binding: Assess the extent of the chalk-like drawing appearance across the image against the input image. Do not treat unrelated changes as progress or require a specific artistic technique.

nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly fulfill the request to turn the image into a drawing made from chalk?
nodes.criteria: Using only the support findings, mark complete if the image as a whole is rendered as a chalk-made drawing. Mark partial if there is evidence of some chalk-drawing progress but the whole-image transformation is incomplete. Mark absent if there is sufficient evidence of no requested chalk-drawing progress; unrelated edits alone are absent. Mark unknown when required evidence is insufficient or unresolved. A failed check does not by itself mean absent if another check establishes partial progress; unknown evidence remains unresolved.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is truncated/ambiguous, and its criterion appears to collapse “chalk-like treatment across the scene” into complete fulfillment. The edited image does show a broad, softened, grainy drawing effect, but the traces do not establish that it convincingly reads as a drawing made from chalk; they mostly repeat the same broad impression, and the reference label is only an aggregate constraint, not proof of a specific missing feature. Refine the typed criterion to distinguish evidence of chalk-medium appearance from generic blur/grain or painterly stylization, and require the support findings to cite visible cues and any remaining photographic or non-chalk appearance across the image. Preserve partial when there is genuine chalk-like progress but whole-image fulfillment is not established; do not infer absence from uncertainty. The checks are valid and queried with no transport or dependency failures, so investigate semantic calibration and evidence quality rather than execution.
s2: The binding is truncated and the node treats scene-wide coverage as sufficient for completion. Clarify that it must assess both extent and whether the visible result reads as a chalk-made drawing, distinguishing chalk-like surface cues from generic blur, grain, or softened photographic detail. In this image, the treatment spans the scene, but the giraffes retain detailed photographic-looking contours and texture while the background is heavily smeared; require evidence that compares these regions and identifies any remaining non-chalk appearance before concluding the transformation is complete. Keep genuine progress distinct from full fulfillment, and do not use uncertainty alone to infer absence. The traces are valid and queried with no transport or dependency failures, so focus on criterion calibration and evidence quality.
s1: Repair the binding so it is complete and unambiguous, and make this support node assess evidence for the requested whole-image transformation rather than treating any chalk-like effect as fulfillment. Distinguish chalk-medium drawing cues from generic blur, grain, or smearing; ask for concrete visual evidence across both foreground subjects and background, including any regions that still look photographic or otherwise not chalk-drawn. Here, the background is strongly softened and smeared, while the giraffes retain comparatively crisp, detailed contours and patterning: weigh that uneven progress against the instruction to turn the image into a chalk drawing. Preserve partial when there is visible progress but complete transformation is not established; do not infer absence from uncertainty or force a label from the aggregate reference alone. The trace is valid, queried, and has no dependency or transport failure, so focus on criterion calibration and evidence quality.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not compose cleanly. s1 asks only for broad chalk-like appearance, while s3 separately tests drawing-like rendering; s2 then tests whole-image coverage but is activated even when s3 is unknown or fails. Its criteria can label a partial effect as fail without establishing that no requested progress occurred, and the fulfillment rule does not clearly distinguish that known partial progress from absence when support findings conflict or remain unresolved. The readout therefore lacks a reliable, non-overlapping mapping of the available evidence to complete, partial, absent, or unknown.

transaction.reason: Add a distinct nested check for whether the result reads as a chalk drawing rather than a scene-wide grainy or softened filter. This investigates the missing distinction without treating the aggregate reference as atomic truth; the readout must allow supported partial progress and avoid counting correlated observations as independent confirmation.

actions.question: Does the edited image read as a chalk drawing, rather than mainly as a softened or blurred image with grain?
actions.criteria: Pass if the scene’s forms and edges visibly have a drawing-like chalk rendering, not merely a chalk-like surface texture or haze. Fail if it remains primarily photographic or blurred with only a texture effect. Unknown if the visual evidence is insufficient to distinguish these.
actions.binding: Compare the edited image with the source. Judge the strength and consistency of drawing-like chalk marks across subjects and background; recognizable forms alone do not decide the result. Use the ancestor observation as context, but inspect this proposition independently.

actions.criteria: Using all saved support findings, mark complete only when evidence establishes both a chalk-drawing rendering and whole-image transformation. Mark partial when there is evidence of requested chalk-drawing progress but the result remains substantially photographic, is only a texture/filter effect, or otherwise falls short of a complete drawing transformation. Mark absent only when evidence establishes no requested chalk-drawing progress; unrelated edits alone are absent. Mark unknown when necessary evidence is insufficient or unresolved. Treat s1, s3, and s2 as related observations, not independent corroboration; scene-wide coverage or a chalk-like texture alone does not establish completion. A negative finding about drawing-like rendering does not erase separately evidenced progress.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide a reliable composition for the requested extent. s1 can pass on a merely chalk-like appearance, while s3 and s2 are activated even when their parent fails or is unknown; s2 can then label a partial effect as fail, and the fulfillment rule treats any fail as evidence of incompleteness. This risks converting insufficient or non-progress evidence into partial rather than keeping it unresolved or absent. The readout also does not explicitly map the available findings to absent versus unknown when evidence is insufficient to establish progress. The program therefore does not preserve the rubric’s required distinction among complete, partial, no progress, and unresolved.

The support checks do not preserve the requested property reliably. s1 and s3 allow a chalk-like texture or softness to count as progress, while s2 can pass on whole-image coverage without establishing that the result reads as a drawing. The fulfillment rule then treats evidence of chalk-like progress plus a negative drawing-rendering finding as partial, even though the support criteria do not distinguish genuine requested progress from a merely photographic texture effect. This permits unsupported partial credit and leaves the requested chalk-drawing property insufficiently evidenced.

The support checks do not reliably preserve the requested extent distinction. s2 treats evidence of “only a partial chalk effect” as a fail, but that is evidence of some requested progress and should support a partial fulfillment, not a no-progress finding. The fulfillment criteria say partial requires genuine chalk-drawing progress, yet s1 can pass on a merely chalk-like appearance and s3 can fail because the result does not read as a chalk drawing; the criteria do not clearly resolve that combination as partial versus absent. Thus the readout can erase progress or leave it unresolved despite the checks’ intended evidence. The program otherwise captures the requested chalk-drawing transformation without imposing a particular technique.
